deviation: The draft says the DPA "has been or will be executed alongside this Agreement", so personal data could be processed before a DPA is signed. The standard requires a signed DPA before any processing, and the playbook requires the Arcadia DPA before go-live. The draft also drops the "documented instructions" requirement and doesn't say the DPA must be Arcadia's form. There is no fallback, so this is worse than the playbook allows. The DPA-prevails and security incident language is acceptable.
suggested_text: 7.1 The Parties acknowledge that the Services involve the processing of Personal Data of the Customer's customers and employees. The Supplier shall process Personal Data only on the Customer's documented instructions and in accordance with applicable data protection law. The Supplier shall execute the Customer's Data Processing Agreement ("DPA") before any Personal Data is processed and in any event before go-live, and shall not process Personal Data until the DPA has been executed. In the event of conflict regarding Personal Data, the DPA prevails. 7.2 The Supplier shall maintain appropriate administrative, technical and physical safeguards designed to protect Customer Data against Security Incidents. In the event of a Security Incident, the Supplier shall notify the Customer as provided in Section 3.4, take prompt steps to contain and remediate it, and cooperate with the Customer's reasonable requests and any legally required notifications.
